newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia announces surprise rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Australia announces surprise rate cut.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia on Wednesday shocked financial markets with a cut in official interest rates of 0.5 percentage points to 6 percent.
Rates were last cut Nov. 6 when the official cash rate was brought down to 6.5 percent from 7 percent.
"This reduction essentially reflects a further improvement in the inflationary outlook," Reserve Bank Gov. Ian MacFarlane said.

MacFarlane said the bank now expected inflation to stay below 2.5 percent for the remainder of 1996/97, citing the strength in the Australian dollar and recent national accounts data which suggested actual inflation could fall further.

The Australian dollar fell sharply in hectic morning trade after the bank's surprise move. In early trading the local dollar had tumbled to 79.63 cents (U.S.) from an early 80.18 cents and 80.23 cents late on Tuesday.
But MacFarlane warned that if wages were to rise appreciably, interest rates would also rise, referring back to the bank's 1994 decisions to hike rates three times to control inflation.
"Monetary policy would, in such circumstances, be set to preserve the favourable inflation outlook," MacFarlane said.
Stunned financial markets agreed with the bank's inflation outlook, but had expected it to keep monetary policy on hold until early 1997 when the next inflation data is released.
